calcium_arrest_routine_adult.doc: Part 9: Adult Advanced Life Support, 2025 AHA Guidelines for CPR and ECC (Wigginton et al, Circulation 2025;152(suppl 2):S538-S577, doi:10.1161/CIR.0000000000001376)
calcium_arrest_routine_adult.section: 11 Nonvasopressor Medications, rec 4 and supportive text
calcium_arrest_routine_adult.says: Routine calcium is not recommended. Trials (including calcium given right after the first epinephrine) showed no survival or neurological benefit, with a trend toward harm. | Suspected hyperkalemia (2b, C-LD - see calcium_hyperkalemia_arrest),Calcium-channel-blocker poisoning (2a, C-EO),Beta-blocker poisoning (2b, C-EO),Cardiac arrest while on IV magnesium sulfate in pregnancy (2a, C-EO),Hypocalcaemia from massive transfusion (trauma protocols - see calcium_massive_transfusion)
calcium_arrest_routine_adult.changedIn2025: LOE upgraded from B-NR (2020) to B-R after the RCTs reviewed in the 2023 focused update; class unchanged. 2020 AHA Part 3 Adult BLS/ALS (Panchal et al, Circulation 2020;142:S366-S468, doi:10.1161/CIR.0000000000000916)

calcium_hyperkalemia_arrest.doc: Part 10: Adult and Pediatric Special Circumstances of Resuscitation, 2025 AHA Guidelines (Cao et al, Circulation 2025;152(suppl 2):S578-S672, doi:10.1161/CIR.0000000000001380)
calcium_hyperkalemia_arrest.says: The effectiveness of IV calcium in hyperkalemic arrest is not well established: the support is historical animal and case data, and a pig RCT showed no ROSC benefit. It remains the listed exception to 'no routine calcium'. |  | AHA 2025 gives no dose. ERC 2025 (cardiac arrest in pregnancy table) lists 10 mL of 10% calcium chloride IV for magnesium overdose, low calcium or hyperkalaemia.
calcium_hyperkalemia_arrest.changedIn2025: Downgraded from 1 C-LD ('IV calcium should be administered', 2020) to 2b C-LD ('not well established'). 2020 AHA Part 3 Adult BLS/ALS (Panchal et al, Circulation 2020;142:S366-S468, doi:10.1161/CIR.0000000000000916)

calcium_ccb_poisoning.doc: Part 10: Adult and Pediatric Special Circumstances of Resuscitation, 2025 AHA Guidelines (Cao et al, Circulation 2025;152(suppl 2):S578-S672, doi:10.1161/CIR.0000000000001380)
calcium_ccb_poisoning.says: Calcium is reasonable (2a, C-EO); high-dose insulin (1, B-NR) and vasopressors (1, C-LD) are the stronger recommendations; ECLS if refractory. |  | Calcium chloride 2000 mg (20 mL of 10%) adult, 20 mg/kg child; or calcium gluconate 6000 mg (60 mL of 10%) adult, 60 mg/kg child; then infusion titrated to BP (Table 4).

calcium_massive_transfusion.doc: AAST/ACS-COT Clinical protocol for damage-control resuscitation for the adult trauma patient (LaGrone et al, J Trauma Acute Care Surg 2024;96(3), doi:10.1097/TA.0000000000004088)
calcium_massive_transfusion.says: Hypocalcaemia is common and linked to coagulopathy and death; protocols target ionized calcium above 1-1.2 mmol/L. Military guidance gives 1 g of calcium with the first unit and at least after 4 units. No prospective trial shows better outcomes. |  | 1 g calcium (military guidance, per AAST protocol); calcium gluconate 4 g over 4 h studied.

pals_calcium_routine.doc: Part 8: Pediatric Advanced Life Support, 2025 AHA/AAP Guidelines (Lasa et al, Circulation 2025;152(suppl 2):S479-S537, doi:10.1161/CIR.0000000000001368)
pals_calcium_routine.section: 7.2 Drug Administration During Cardiac Arrest, rec 6 and supportive text
pals_calcium_routine.says: Not recommended routinely; associated with lower survival to discharge in pediatric IHCA (possible time bias). | Hypocalcemia,Calcium-channel-blocker overdose,Hyperkalemia
pals_calcium_routine.changedIn2025: Reclassified from 3: Harm (2020) to 3: No Benefit; the 2020 exception list also named hypermagnesemia. 2020 AHA Part 4 Pediatric BLS/ALS (Topjian et al, Circulation 2020;142:S469-S523, doi:10.1161/CIR.0000000000000901)

bicarbonate_arrest_routine_adult.doc: Part 9: Adult Advanced Life Support, 2025 AHA Guidelines for CPR and ECC (Wigginton et al, Circulation 2025;152(suppl 2):S538-S577, doi:10.1161/CIR.0000000000001376)
bicarbonate_arrest_routine_adult.section: 11 Nonvasopressor Medications, rec 5 and supportive text
bicarbonate_arrest_routine_adult.says: Routine sodium bicarbonate is not recommended. Recent observational data in prehospital PEA/asystole hint at benefit, but resuscitation-time bias makes it uninterpretable; equipoise for new trials only. | Suspected hyperkalemia (2b, C-EO),Tricyclic/tetracyclic antidepressant cardiotoxicity (1, B-NR adults; 2a, C-LD children),Other sodium-channel-blocker cardiotoxicity (2a, C-EO),Wide-complex tachycardia from local-anesthetic toxicity (2a, C-EO)

bicarbonate_sodium_channel_blocker.doc: Part 10: Adult and Pediatric Special Circumstances of Resuscitation, 2025 AHA Guidelines (Cao et al, Circulation 2025;152(suppl 2):S578-S672, doi:10.1161/CIR.0000000000001380)
bicarbonate_sodium_channel_blocker.says: Bicarbonate should be used for TCA cardiotoxicity in adults (1, B-NR) and is reasonable in children (2a, C-LD) and for other sodium-channel blockers (2a, C-EO); hyperventilation with it is reasonable in ventilated patients. Lidocaine may be reasonable for class Ia/Ic antiarrhythmic toxicity (2b, C-EO). |  | 50-150 mEq adult, 1-3 mEq/kg child; then 150 mEq/L infusion at 1-3 mL/kg/h (Table 4).

bicarbonate_hyperkalemia_arrest.doc: Part 10: Adult and Pediatric Special Circumstances of Resuscitation, 2025 AHA Guidelines (Cao et al, Circulation 2025;152(suppl 2):S578-S672, doi:10.1161/CIR.0000000000001380)
bicarbonate_hyperkalemia_arrest.says: Effectiveness not well established. It shifts potassium into cells; one pig RCT improved ROSC; human data are weak. |
bicarbonate_hyperkalemia_arrest.changedIn2025: New recommendation (2020 had none for bicarbonate in hyperkalemic arrest). 2020 AHA Part 3 Adult BLS/ALS (Panchal et al, Circulation 2020;142:S366-S468, doi:10.1161/CIR.0000000000000916)

pals_bicarbonate_routine.doc: Part 8: Pediatric Advanced Life Support, 2025 AHA/AAP Guidelines (Lasa et al, Circulation 2025;152(suppl 2):S479-S537, doi:10.1161/CIR.0000000000001368)
pals_bicarbonate_routine.section: 7.2 Drug Administration During Cardiac Arrest, rec 5 and supportive text
pals_bicarbonate_routine.says: Not recommended routinely; pediatric IHCA meta-analysis associated it with lower survival (possibly resuscitation-time bias). | Sodium-channel-blocker toxicity (eg tricyclics, cocaine),Hyperkalemia
pals_bicarbonate_routine.changedIn2025: Reclassified from 3: Harm (2020) to 3: No Benefit, B-NR. 2020 AHA Part 4 Pediatric BLS/ALS (Topjian et al, Circulation 2020;142:S469-S523, doi:10.1161/CIR.0000000000000901)

bicarbonate_trauma_acidosis.doc: AAST/ACS-COT Clinical protocol for damage-control resuscitation for the adult trauma patient (LaGrone et al, J Trauma Acute Care Surg 2024;96(3), doi:10.1097/TA.0000000000004088)
bicarbonate_trauma_acidosis.says: Bicarbonate for trauma acidaemia is not well studied; no benefit above pH 7.2 and questionable below. Correct acidosis by stopping the bleeding and giving blood. | Haemorrhage control,Blood product resuscitation

blood_vs_crystalloid_trauma_adult.doc: AAST/ACS-COT Clinical protocol for damage-control resuscitation for the adult trauma patient (LaGrone et al, J Trauma Acute Care Surg 2024;96(3), doi:10.1097/TA.0000000000004088)
blood_vs_crystalloid_trauma_adult.section: Isotonic Crystalloid Resuscitation; Correct Trauma-Induced Coagulopathy
blood_vs_crystalloid_trauma_adult.says: Resuscitate with blood products (whole blood or balanced 1:1:1), not crystalloid. More crystalloid is linked to ARDS (each extra 500 mL in 6 h, +9%), and TCCC no longer recommends crystalloid in haemorrhagic shock. Stop the bleeding first. | Haemorrhage control (tourniquet, packing, pelvic binder),Massive transfusion protocol,TXA within 3 h

txa_trauma.doc: CRASH-2 trial (Lancet 2010;376:23-32, doi:10.1016/S0140-6736(10)60835-5) and its time-to-treatment analysis (Lancet 2011;377:1096-1101, doi:10.1016/S0140-6736(11)60278-X); AAST/ACS-COT Clinical protocol for damage-control resuscitation for the adult trauma patient (LaGrone et al, J Trauma Acute Care Surg 2024;96(3), doi:10.1097/TA.0000000000004088); European Resuscitation Council Guidelines 2025: Special Circumstances in Resuscitation (Lott et al, Resuscitation 2025;215 Suppl 1:110753)
txa_trauma.section: CRASH-2 results; AAST/ACS-COT 'Tranexamic Acid'; ERC traumatic cardiac arrest - hypovolaemia
txa_trauma.says: Give TXA as early as possible and within 3 hours of injury. In CRASH-2 it cut deaths from bleeding when given within 1 h (RR 0.68) or 1-3 h (RR 0.79); given after 3 h it increased death from bleeding (RR 1.44). Data in isolated head injury are mixed. | Not after 3 hours from injury | 1 g IV over 10 min, then 1 g over 8 h.

magnesium_arrest_routine_adult.doc: Part 9: Adult Advanced Life Support, 2025 AHA Guidelines for CPR and ECC (Wigginton et al, Circulation 2025;152(suppl 2):S538-S577, doi:10.1161/CIR.0000000000001376)
magnesium_arrest_routine_adult.section: 11 Nonvasopressor Medications, rec 6 and supportive text
magnesium_arrest_routine_adult.says: Routine magnesium is not recommended: it did not improve ROSC, survival or neurological outcome in any presenting rhythm, and was not useful for monomorphic VT. | Torsades de pointes (polymorphic VT with a long QT) - see magnesium_torsades

magnesium_torsades.doc: Part 9: Adult Advanced Life Support, 2025 AHA Guidelines for CPR and ECC (Wigginton et al, Circulation 2025;152(suppl 2):S538-S577, doi:10.1161/CIR.0000000000001376)
magnesium_torsades.section: 16 Polymorphic Ventricular Tachycardia, rec 2 and supportive text
magnesium_torsades.says: Magnesium may be considered to suppress recurrences of torsades. Also correct electrolytes (especially low potassium) and stop QT-prolonging drugs; for bradycardia- or pause-dependent torsades seek expert help for overdrive pacing or isoproterenol. |  | AHA 2025 gives no dose. ERC 2025 (cardiac arrest in pregnancy table) lists magnesium 2 g IV for polymorphic VT.
magnesium_torsades.changedIn2025: Wording now 'recurrences of' polymorphic VT with long QT; class/LOE unchanged (2b, C-LD). 2020 AHA Part 3 Adult BLS/ALS (Panchal et al, Circulation 2020;142:S366-S468, doi:10.1161/CIR.0000000000000916)

atropine_arrest.doc: Part 9: Adult Advanced Life Support, 2025 AHA Guidelines for CPR and ECC (Wigginton et al, Circulation 2025;152(suppl 2):S538-S577, doi:10.1161/CIR.0000000000001376)
atropine_arrest.section: Figure 2 Adult Cardiac Arrest Algorithm; 19 Bradycardia supportive text
atropine_arrest.says: Atropine is not part of the 2025 adult cardiac arrest algorithm. The 2025 text notes one OHCA study associating atropine-after-epinephrine with survival to admission and one IHCA study showing no survival benefit; no recommendation to use it. | Bradycardia WITH a pulse and compromise

atropine_bradycardia_adult.doc: Part 9: Adult Advanced Life Support, 2025 AHA Guidelines for CPR and ECC (Wigginton et al, Circulation 2025;152(suppl 2):S538-S577, doi:10.1161/CIR.0000000000001376)
atropine_bradycardia_adult.section: 19 Initial Management of Bradycardia, rec 2; Figure 8 Adult Bradycardia With a Pulse Algorithm
atropine_bradycardia_adult.says: Atropine is reasonable to raise the rate in unstable bradycardia (typically HR <50) while reversible causes are treated. |  | 1 mg IV bolus, repeat every 3-5 min, maximum total 3 mg. It is a bolus, never an infusion.

epinephrine_nonshockable_timing.doc: Part 9: Adult Advanced Life Support, 2025 AHA Guidelines for CPR and ECC (Wigginton et al, Circulation 2025;152(suppl 2):S538-S577, doi:10.1161/CIR.0000000000001376)
epinephrine_nonshockable_timing.says: In a nonshockable arrest give the first epinephrine as soon as feasible (algorithm: 'Epinephrine ASAP'). |
epinephrine_nonshockable_timing.changedIn2025: LOE upgraded from C-LD (2020) to B-NR; class unchanged (2a). 2020 AHA Part 3 Adult BLS/ALS (Panchal et al, Circulation 2020;142:S366-S468, doi:10.1161/CIR.0000000000000916)

pals_atropine_bradycardia.doc: Part 8: Pediatric Advanced Life Support, 2025 AHA/AAP Guidelines (Lasa et al, Circulation 2025;152(suppl 2):S479-S537, doi:10.1161/CIR.0000000000001368)
pals_atropine_bradycardia.section: 18 Management of Bradycardia, recs 1-2 and supportive text; Figure 6 Pediatric Bradycardia With a Pulse Algorithm
pals_atropine_bradycardia.says: Atropine is recommended only when the bradycardia is from increased vagal tone or primary AV block, NOT from hypoxia. Hypoxic bradycardia is treated with ventilation and oxygen; if HR stays <60 with compromise despite effective ventilation, start CPR (1, C-EO). | Oxygen and ventilation for hypoxic bradycardia,CPR if HR <60 with poor perfusion despite ventilation,Epinephrine if it persists | 0.02 mg/kg IV/IO, may repeat once; minimum 0.1 mg, maximum single dose 0.5 mg.

pals_epinephrine_nonshockable_timing.doc: Part 8: Pediatric Advanced Life Support, 2025 AHA/AAP Guidelines (Lasa et al, Circulation 2025;152(suppl 2):S479-S537, doi:10.1161/CIR.0000000000001368)
pals_epinephrine_nonshockable_timing.section: 7.2 Drug Administration During Cardiac Arrest, rec 1; Figure 2
pals_epinephrine_nonshockable_timing.says: Give the first epinephrine as early as possible. |  | 0.01 mg/kg IV/IO (0.1 mL/kg of 0.1 mg/mL), max 1 mg.
pals_epinephrine_nonshockable_timing.changedIn2025: 2020 said 'within 5 min of starting compressions' (2a, C-LD); 2025 says 'as early as possible' for nonshockable rhythms. 2020 AHA Part 4 Pediatric BLS/ALS (Topjian et al, Circulation 2020;142:S469-S523, doi:10.1161/CIR.0000000000000901)

drug_instead_of_cardioversion_unstable.doc: Part 9: Adult Advanced Life Support, 2025 AHA Guidelines for CPR and ECC (Wigginton et al, Circulation 2025;152(suppl 2):S538-S577, doi:10.1161/CIR.0000000000001376)
drug_instead_of_cardioversion_unstable.section: 15 Wide-Complex Tachycardia rec 1; 17 Regular Narrow-Complex Tachycardia rec 3; Figure 6 Adult Tachyarrhythmia With a Pulse Algorithm
drug_instead_of_cardioversion_unstable.says: An unstable wide- or narrow-complex tachycardia needs immediate synchronized cardioversion (sedate if feasible). Drugs are for stable patients; the algorithm allows adenosine only for a regular narrow rhythm while preparing to cardiovert. | Synchronized cardioversion now

adenosine_regular_nct.doc: Part 9: Adult Advanced Life Support, 2025 AHA Guidelines for CPR and ECC (Wigginton et al, Circulation 2025;152(suppl 2):S538-S577, doi:10.1161/CIR.0000000000001376)
adenosine_regular_nct.section: 17 Regular Narrow-Complex Tachycardia, recs 1-2 and supportive text; Figure 6 doses box
adenosine_regular_nct.says: Vagal manoeuvres (1, B-R) and adenosine (1, B-R) are the first treatments. Adenosine is contraindicated in asthma (bronchospasm); 1 mg may be enough with a central line or after heart transplant. |  | 6 mg rapid IV push with saline flush; 12 mg if needed.

pals_adenosine_svt.doc: Part 8: Pediatric Advanced Life Support, 2025 AHA/AAP Guidelines (Lasa et al, Circulation 2025;152(suppl 2):S479-S537, doi:10.1161/CIR.0000000000001368)
pals_adenosine_svt.section: 19.1 Treatment of SVT With a Pulse, recs 1-4; Figure 7 Pediatric Tachyarrhythmia With a Pulse Algorithm
pals_adenosine_svt.says: Try vagal stimulation first if there is no cardiopulmonary compromise (1, C-LD); adenosine is recommended if IV/IO access is ready (1, C-LD). With compromise: adenosine if access is present, or synchronized cardioversion 0.5-1 J/kg then 2 J/kg (2a, C-LD). |  | 0.1 mg/kg rapid push (max 6 mg) with flush; repeat 0.2 mg/kg (max 12 mg).
pals_adenosine_svt.changedIn2025: Vagal stimulation first upgraded from 2a C-LD (2020) to 1 C-LD. 2020 AHA Part 4 Pediatric BLS/ALS (Topjian et al, Circulation 2020;142:S469-S523, doi:10.1161/CIR.0000000000000901)

pals_epinephrine_bradycardia.doc: Part 8: Pediatric Advanced Life Support, 2025 AHA/AAP Guidelines (Lasa et al, Circulation 2025;152(suppl 2):S479-S537, doi:10.1161/CIR.0000000000001368)
pals_epinephrine_bradycardia.says: Give epinephrine IV/IO when bradycardia with cardiopulmonary compromise persists after correcting other factors (eg hypoxia). Pacing may be considered for complete heart block or sinus node dysfunction unresponsive to CPR (2b, C-EO). |  | 0.01 mg/kg IV/IO (0.1 mg/mL), max 1 mg.
pals_epinephrine_bradycardia.changedIn2025: 2020 allowed the endotracheal route if IV/IO was unavailable; 2025 says IV/IO only. 2020 AHA Part 4 Pediatric BLS/ALS (Topjian et al, Circulation 2020;142:S469-S523, doi:10.1161/CIR.0000000000000901)

adenosine_af.doc: Part 9: Adult Advanced Life Support, 2025 AHA Guidelines for CPR and ECC (Wigginton et al, Circulation 2025;152(suppl 2):S538-S577, doi:10.1161/CIR.0000000000001376)
adenosine_af.section: 17 supportive text (adenosine); 18.1-18.2 Atrial Fibrillation or Flutter with RVR
adenosine_af.says: Adenosine only blocks the AV node briefly (it unmasks flutter or fibrillation); it is not an AF treatment. For rate control give an IV beta-blocker or nondihydropyridine calcium-channel blocker (1, B-NR), or IV amiodarone in the critically ill (2a, B-NR); cardiovert if unstable (1, C-LD). | IV beta-blocker or diltiazem/verapamil for rate control,Amiodarone if critically ill,Synchronized cardioversion (>=200 J) if unstable

adenosine_wct.doc: Part 9: Adult Advanced Life Support, 2025 AHA Guidelines for CPR and ECC (Wigginton et al, Circulation 2025;152(suppl 2):S538-S577, doi:10.1161/CIR.0000000000001376)
adenosine_wct.section: 15 Wide-Complex Tachycardia, recs 4 and 6 and supportive text
adenosine_wct.says: Only for a STABLE, REGULAR, MONOMORPHIC wide-complex tachycardia, to treat or aid diagnosis (2b, B-NR). Adenosine should NOT be given for an unstable, irregularly irregular or polymorphic wide-complex tachycardia (3: Harm, C-LD): it will not stop VT and can cause hypotension or VF. | Unstable: synchronized cardioversion,Polymorphic: unsynchronized shock,Irregular (possible pre-excited AF): cardioversion / expert help

polymorphic_vt_shock_first.doc: Part 9: Adult Advanced Life Support, 2025 AHA Guidelines for CPR and ECC (Wigginton et al, Circulation 2025;152(suppl 2):S538-S577, doi:10.1161/CIR.0000000000001376)
polymorphic_vt_shock_first.section: 16 Polymorphic Ventricular Tachycardia, rec 1; Top 10 message 8
polymorphic_vt_shock_first.says: Polymorphic VT is always unstable: give an immediate unsynchronized (defibrillation-energy) shock; drugs are for preventing recurrence, not for the running rhythm. |

antiarrhythmic_in_torsades.doc: Part 9: Adult Advanced Life Support, 2025 AHA Guidelines for CPR and ECC (Wigginton et al, Circulation 2025;152(suppl 2):S538-S577, doi:10.1161/CIR.0000000000001376)
antiarrhythmic_in_torsades.section: 16 Polymorphic Ventricular Tachycardia, supportive text for rec 2
antiarrhythmic_in_torsades.says: Antiarrhythmics given for torsades may prolong the QT further and promote the arrhythmia; acute beta-blockers can precipitate torsades by causing bradycardia. Lidocaine/amiodarone are the options only when the QT is NOT prolonged. | Magnesium (2b, C-LD),Correct potassium,Overdrive pacing or isoproterenol with expert consultation,Stop the QT-prolonging drug

antiarrhythmic_nonshockable.doc: Part 9: Adult Advanced Life Support, 2025 AHA Guidelines for CPR and ECC (Wigginton et al, Circulation 2025;152(suppl 2):S538-S577, doi:10.1161/CIR.0000000000001376)
antiarrhythmic_nonshockable.says: Antiarrhythmics appear only on the VF/pVT side of the arrest algorithm; the asystole/PEA path is CPR, epinephrine and reversible causes. (Derived from the algorithm: there is no statement recommending them in a nonshockable rhythm.) | VF/pVT refractory to shocks

amiodarone_lidocaine_refractory_vf.doc: Part 9: Adult Advanced Life Support, 2025 AHA Guidelines for CPR and ECC (Wigginton et al, Circulation 2025;152(suppl 2):S538-S577, doi:10.1161/CIR.0000000000001376)
amiodarone_lidocaine_refractory_vf.section: 11 Nonvasopressor Medications, rec 1 and supportive text; Figure 2 drug-therapy box
amiodarone_lidocaine_refractory_vf.says: Amiodarone or lidocaine may be considered for shock-refractory VF/pVT (algorithm: after the 3rd shock). They improved survival to admission, not to discharge; benefit looks time-dependent (bystander- or EMS-witnessed arrests). Neither is preferred over the other. | Only for a shockable rhythm that persists after shocks; not for PEA/asystole or a perfusing rhythm | Amiodarone 300 mg IV/IO bolus, then 150 mg; OR lidocaine 1-1.5 mg/kg, then 0.5-0.75 mg/kg.

pals_amiodarone_lidocaine.doc: Part 8: Pediatric Advanced Life Support, 2025 AHA/AAP Guidelines (Lasa et al, Circulation 2025;152(suppl 2):S479-S537, doi:10.1161/CIR.0000000000001368)
pals_amiodarone_lidocaine.section: 7.2 Drug Administration During Cardiac Arrest, rec 4; Figure 2 drug box
pals_amiodarone_lidocaine.says: Either amiodarone or lidocaine may be considered; propensity-matched data show no difference between them. |  | Amiodarone 5 mg/kg IV/IO bolus (max 300 mg), may repeat up to 3 doses (max 150 mg for later doses); OR lidocaine 1 mg/kg.
pals_amiodarone_lidocaine.changedIn2025: Class/LOE unchanged (2020 wording 'may be used'); 2025 algorithm adds per-dose caps for amiodarone. 2020 AHA Part 4 Pediatric BLS/ALS (Topjian et al, Circulation 2020;142:S469-S523, doi:10.1161/CIR.0000000000000901)

epinephrine_dopamine_infusion_bradycardi.doc: Part 9: Adult Advanced Life Support, 2025 AHA Guidelines for CPR and ECC (Wigginton et al, Circulation 2025;152(suppl 2):S538-S577, doi:10.1161/CIR.0000000000001376)
epinephrine_dopamine_infusion_bradycardi.section: 19 Initial Management of Bradycardia, rec 4 and supportive text; Figure 8 doses box
epinephrine_dopamine_infusion_bradycardi.says: If atropine fails, an epinephrine or dopamine infusion or transcutaneous pacing may be effective while transvenous pacing is arranged. Push-dose epinephrine for bradycardia has little supporting data, and dosing errors are reported. |  | Epinephrine infusion 2-10 mcg/min; dopamine 5-20 mcg/kg/min, titrated to response.
epinephrine_dopamine_infusion_bradycardi.changedIn2025: 2025 names dopamine alongside epinephrine (2020: 'eg, epinephrine'); class/LOE unchanged. 2020 AHA Part 3 Adult BLS/ALS (Panchal et al, Circulation 2020;142:S366-S468, doi:10.1161/CIR.0000000000000916)

antiarrhythmic_stable_wct.doc: Part 9: Adult Advanced Life Support, 2025 AHA Guidelines for CPR and ECC (Wigginton et al, Circulation 2025;152(suppl 2):S538-S577, doi:10.1161/CIR.0000000000001376)
antiarrhythmic_stable_wct.section: 15 Wide-Complex Tachycardia, rec 3 and supportive text; Figure 6 doses box
antiarrhythmic_stable_wct.says: IV amiodarone, procainamide or sotalol may be considered. Lidocaine is less effective for VT at tolerated rates. Do not combine them (additive arrhythmia risk); keep a defibrillator ready. Procainamide: avoid if QT prolonged or heart failure. |  | Procainamide 20-50 mg/min until arrhythmia suppressed, hypotension, QRS widens >50% or 17 mg/kg given; maintenance 1-4 mg/min. Amiodarone 150 mg over 10 min, repeat if VT recurs, then 1 mg/min for 6 h.

epinephrine_arrest_dose_with_pulse.doc: Part 9: Adult Advanced Life Support, 2025 AHA Guidelines for CPR and ECC (Wigginton et al, Circulation 2025;152(suppl 2):S538-S577, doi:10.1161/CIR.0000000000001376)
epinephrine_arrest_dose_with_pulse.section: 19 Initial Management of Bradycardia, supportive text; Figures 2 and 8
epinephrine_arrest_dose_with_pulse.says: The 1 mg bolus is the pulseless-arrest dose. With a pulse, the algorithm uses an infusion of 2-10 mcg/min; push-dose epinephrine lacks data for bradycardia and carries reported dosing errors. | Epinephrine infusion 2-10 mcg/min,Atropine first for bradycardia,Pacing

nrp_epinephrine_intravascular.doc: Part 5: Neonatal Resuscitation, 2025 AHA/AAP Guidelines (Lee et al, Circulation 2025;152(suppl 2):S385-S423, doi:10.1161/CIR.0000000000001367)
nrp_epinephrine_intravascular.section: 15 Epinephrine, recs 1 and 4 and synopsis; 13.1 rec 1; Figure 2 Neonatal Resuscitation Algorithm
nrp_epinephrine_intravascular.says: Give intravascular (UVC or IO) epinephrine when the heart rate stays below 60/min after ventilation has been optimized (including an alternative airway) and chest compressions given; follow with a 3 mL saline flush. | Ventilation that moves the chest comes first,Compressions only if HR <60 despite 30 s of effective ventilation (1, C-EO) | 0.01-0.03 mg/kg IV/IO, every 3-5 min if HR <60 (2b, C-LD).
nrp_epinephrine_intravascular.changedIn2025: Upgraded from 2b C-LD (2020) to 1 B-NR. 2020 AHA/AAP Part 5 Neonatal Resuscitation (Aziz et al, Pediatrics 2021;147 Suppl 1:e2020038505E)

naloxone_cardiac_arrest_adult.doc: Part 10: Adult and Pediatric Special Circumstances of Resuscitation, 2025 AHA Guidelines (Cao et al, Circulation 2025;152(suppl 2):S578-S672, doi:10.1161/CIR.0000000000001380)
naloxone_cardiac_arrest_adult.section: 21.11 Opioid Overdose, recs 4-5 and supportive text
naloxone_cardiac_arrest_adult.says: Naloxone may be reasonable only if it does not interfere with high-quality compression-ventilation CPR. It is unlikely to help without circulation and does not reverse VF; start CPR and continue standard ALS first. | High-quality CPR with ventilation (1, C-EO: do not delay resuscitation for naloxone),Epinephrine per the arrest algorithm
naloxone_cardiac_arrest_adult.changedIn2025: New explicit 2b recommendation; 2020 said only that standard resuscitation takes priority over naloxone (1, C-EO). Opioid antagonists are now built into the 2025 BLS algorithms (Part 7). 2020 AHA Part 3 Adult BLS/ALS (Panchal et al, Circulation 2020;142:S366-S468, doi:10.1161/CIR.0000000000000916)

naloxone_resp_arrest_pulse.doc: Part 10: Adult and Pediatric Special Circumstances of Resuscitation, 2025 AHA Guidelines (Cao et al, Circulation 2025;152(suppl 2):S578-S672, doi:10.1161/CIR.0000000000001380)
naloxone_resp_arrest_pulse.section: 21.11 Opioid Overdose, recs 1 and 3; Table 4 antidote doses
naloxone_resp_arrest_pulse.says: Ventilate (bag-mask) and give an opioid antagonist such as naloxone. |  | Adult 0.2-2 mg IV/IO/IM or 2-4 mg intranasal, repeat every 2-3 min; child 0.1 mg/kg.
naloxone_resp_arrest_pulse.changedIn2025: Upgraded from 2a B-NR (2020) to 1 B-NR. 2020 AHA Part 3 Adult BLS/ALS (Panchal et al, Circulation 2020;142:S366-S468, doi:10.1161/CIR.0000000000000916)

naloxone_cardiac_arrest_child.doc: Part 10: Adult and Pediatric Special Circumstances of Resuscitation, 2025 AHA Guidelines (Cao et al, Circulation 2025;152(suppl 2):S578-S672, doi:10.1161/CIR.0000000000001380)
naloxone_cardiac_arrest_child.says: As for adults: may be reasonable if it does not interfere with high-quality CPR; evidence extrapolated from adults. |  | 0.1 mg/kg (Table 4).
naloxone_cardiac_arrest_child.changedIn2025: New explicit recommendation in 2025. 2020 AHA Part 4 Pediatric BLS/ALS (Topjian et al, Circulation 2020;142:S469-S523, doi:10.1161/CIR.0000000000000901)

epinephrine_traumatic_arrest.doc: NAEMSP/ACS-COT/ACEP joint position statement: Prehospital management of adults with traumatic out-of-hospital circulatory arrest (Prehosp Emerg Care 2025, doi:10.1080/10903127.2024.2428668; also Ann Emerg Med 2025, doi:10.1016/j.annemergmed.2024.12.015); European Resuscitation Council Guidelines 2025: Special Circumstances in Resuscitation (Lott et al, Resuscitation 2025;215 Suppl 1:110753)
epinephrine_traumatic_arrest.section: Joint statement recommendations (abstract); ERC 'The role of inotropes and vasopressors'
epinephrine_traumatic_arrest.says: Epinephrine should not be used routinely in traumatic arrest and never before the life-saving interventions: haemorrhage control, airway, chest decompression, volume. ERC 2025: the role of vasopressors in traumatic arrest is unclear; at most a bridge while causes are fixed. | Tourniquet/packing, pelvic binder,Bilateral decompression if chest trauma,Blood,Thoracotomy for tamponade/penetrating injury

vasopressors_haemorrhagic_shock.doc: AAST/ACS-COT Clinical protocol for damage-control resuscitation for the adult trauma patient (LaGrone et al, J Trauma Acute Care Surg 2024;96(3), doi:10.1097/TA.0000000000004088)
vasopressors_haemorrhagic_shock.says: Retrospective data link vasopressors in haemorrhagic shock to worse outcomes, partly from under-resuscitation; evidence is insufficient for a firm recommendation. Low-dose vasopressin (AVERT-Shock) reduced blood use without mortality change; vasopressors are considered only when vasoplegia contributes. | Volume with blood,Haemorrhage control

vasopressin_arrest.doc: Part 9: Adult Advanced Life Support, 2025 AHA Guidelines for CPR and ECC (Wigginton et al, Circulation 2025;152(suppl 2):S538-S577, doi:10.1161/CIR.0000000000001376)
vasopressin_arrest.says: Vasopressin, alone or added to epinephrine, offers no advantage as a substitute for epinephrine. | Use epinephrine 1 mg every 3-5 min
vasopressin_arrest.changedIn2025: Reclassified from 2b C-LD ('may be considered but offers no advantage', 2020) to 3: No Benefit, B-R. 2020 AHA Part 3 Adult BLS/ALS (Panchal et al, Circulation 2020;142:S366-S468, doi:10.1161/CIR.0000000000000916)

epinephrine_arrest_adult.doc: Part 9: Adult Advanced Life Support, 2025 AHA Guidelines for CPR and ECC (Wigginton et al, Circulation 2025;152(suppl 2):S538-S577, doi:10.1161/CIR.0000000000001376)
epinephrine_arrest_adult.section: 10 Vasopressor Medications in Adult Cardiac Arrest, recs 1-2; Figure 2 Adult Cardiac Arrest Algorithm
epinephrine_arrest_adult.says: Give epinephrine in adult cardiac arrest. It raises ROSC and short-term survival; no trial shows better neurological survival. |  | 1 mg IV/IO every 3-5 min (2a, B-R); every second 2-minute cycle meets this.

thrombolytic_pe_suspected.doc: Part 10: Adult and Pediatric Special Circumstances of Resuscitation, 2025 AHA Guidelines (Cao et al, Circulation 2025;152(suppl 2):S578-S672, doi:10.1161/CIR.0000000000001380)
thrombolytic_pe_suspected.section: 20.2 Adults in Cardiac Arrest From PE, rec 3 and supportive text
thrombolytic_pe_suspected.says: May be considered when PE is suspected. Two RCTs found no survival benefit from fibrinolytics in undifferentiated cardiac arrest, so it is not a routine arrest drug. | Confirmed or strongly suspected PE
thrombolytic_pe_suspected.changedIn2025: LOE upgraded from C-LD (2020) to B-NR. 2020 AHA Part 3 Adult BLS/ALS (Panchal et al, Circulation 2020;142:S366-S468, doi:10.1161/CIR.0000000000000916)

thrombolytic_pe_confirmed.doc: Part 10: Adult and Pediatric Special Circumstances of Resuscitation, 2025 AHA Guidelines (Cao et al, Circulation 2025;152(suppl 2):S578-S672, doi:10.1161/CIR.0000000000001380)
thrombolytic_pe_confirmed.section: 20.2 Adults in Cardiac Arrest From PE, recs 1-2, 4
thrombolytic_pe_confirmed.says: Systemic fibrinolysis, surgical or percutaneous embolectomy are reasonable; ECLS is reasonable for confirmed or suspected PE (2a, B-NR). Optimal CPR duration after the drug is unclear (2b, C-EO). |
thrombolytic_pe_confirmed.changedIn2025: LOE upgraded from C-LD (2020) to B-NR; ECLS recommendation new. 2020 AHA Part 3 Adult BLS/ALS (Panchal et al, Circulation 2020;142:S366-S468, doi:10.1161/CIR.0000000000000916)

epinephrine_high_dose.doc: Part 9: Adult Advanced Life Support, 2025 AHA Guidelines for CPR and ECC (Wigginton et al, Circulation 2025;152(suppl 2):S538-S577, doi:10.1161/CIR.0000000000001376)
epinephrine_high_dose.section: 10 Vasopressor Medications, rec 6 and supportive text
epinephrine_high_dose.says: High-dose epinephrine is not recommended for routine use. A registry study suggested dosing more often than the standard interval may be harmful. |

pals_epinephrine_interval.doc: Part 8: Pediatric Advanced Life Support, 2025 AHA/AAP Guidelines (Lasa et al, Circulation 2025;152(suppl 2):S479-S537, doi:10.1161/CIR.0000000000001368)
pals_epinephrine_interval.section: 7.2 Drug Administration During Cardiac Arrest, rec 3; Figure 2
pals_epinephrine_interval.says: Epinephrine every 3-5 minutes until ROSC may be reasonable; the optimal interval is unknown. |  | 0.01 mg/kg IV/IO, max 1 mg per dose.
pals_epinephrine_interval.changedIn2025: Downgraded from 2a C-LD (2020) to 2b C-LD. 2020 AHA Part 4 Pediatric BLS/ALS (Topjian et al, Circulation 2020;142:S469-S523, doi:10.1161/CIR.0000000000000901)

naloxone_infusion.doc: Part 10: Adult and Pediatric Special Circumstances of Resuscitation, 2025 AHA Guidelines (Cao et al, Circulation 2025;152(suppl 2):S578-S672, doi:10.1161/CIR.0000000000001380)
naloxone_infusion.section: 21.11 Opioid Overdose following successful response, recs 1-4 and supportive text; Table 4
naloxone_infusion.says: Repeat doses (2a, C-LD adults; 2a, C-EO children) or an IV infusion treat re-sedation; observe until low risk. An infusion is for the patient who has responded, not arrest care. |  | Infusion: two thirds of the waking dose per hour (Table 4).

vascular_access_adult.doc: Part 9: Adult Advanced Life Support, 2025 AHA Guidelines for CPR and ECC (Wigginton et al, Circulation 2025;152(suppl 2):S538-S577, doi:10.1161/CIR.0000000000001376)
vascular_access_adult.section: 9 Vascular Access in Cardiac Arrest Management, recs 1-3
vascular_access_adult.says: Attempt peripheral IV first (1, A); IO is reasonable if IV attempts fail or are not feasible (2a, A); central venous access may be considered by trained staff if both fail (2b, C-LD). Three RCTs found no advantage to IO-first, and ROSC was slightly lower with IO. |
vascular_access_adult.changedIn2025: IV-first upgraded from 2a B-NR to 1 A; IO upgraded from 2b B-NR to 2a A. 2020 AHA Part 3 Adult BLS/ALS (Panchal et al, Circulation 2020;142:S366-S468, doi:10.1161/CIR.0000000000000916)

drug_route_endotracheal_adult.doc: Part 9: Adult Advanced Life Support, 2025 AHA Guidelines for CPR and ECC (Wigginton et al, Circulation 2025;152(suppl 2):S538-S577, doi:10.1161/CIR.0000000000001376)
drug_route_endotracheal_adult.section: Top 10 Take-Home Messages (message 6); 9 Vascular Access, synopsis
drug_route_endotracheal_adult.says: Giving arrest drugs down an endotracheal tube has been removed from the adult guidelines: blood levels are low and unpredictable. Use IV, then IO, then central access. | IV first,IO if IV fails or is not feasible,central venous access by trained staff if both fail
drug_route_endotracheal_adult.changedIn2025: 2020 allowed it as a last resort (2b, C-LD: 'may be considered when other access routes are not available'); 2025 removed it. 2020 AHA Part 3 Adult BLS/ALS (Panchal et al, Circulation 2020;142:S366-S468, doi:10.1161/CIR.0000000000000916)

pals_vascular_access_route.doc: Part 8: Pediatric Advanced Life Support, 2025 AHA/AAP Guidelines (Lasa et al, Circulation 2025;152(suppl 2):S479-S537, doi:10.1161/CIR.0000000000001368)
pals_vascular_access_route.section: 7.1 Drug Administration Methods, recs 1-2 and synopsis; Figure 2 Pediatric Cardiac Arrest Algorithm
pals_vascular_access_route.says: Get IV or IO access rapidly (1, C-LD), choosing by availability and expertise (1, C-EO). IV/IO epinephrine is preferred over the endotracheal route (poor absorption); the 2025 algorithm lists only IV/IO doses. |
pals_vascular_access_route.changedIn2025: The 2020 PALS algorithm gave an endotracheal epinephrine dose (0.1 mg/kg); the 2025 algorithm gives IV/IO only. 2020 AHA Part 4 Pediatric BLS/ALS (Topjian et al, Circulation 2020;142:S469-S523, doi:10.1161/CIR.0000000000000901)

nrp_vascular_access.doc: Part 5: Neonatal Resuscitation, 2025 AHA/AAP Guidelines (Lee et al, Circulation 2025;152(suppl 2):S385-S423, doi:10.1161/CIR.0000000000001367)
nrp_vascular_access.says: An umbilical venous catheter is recommended (1, C-LD); IO can be useful if IV access fails or is not feasible (2a, C-LD). |
nrp_vascular_access.changedIn2025: UVC LOE C-EO to C-LD; IO upgraded from 2b C-EO to 2a C-LD. 2020 AHA/AAP Part 5 Neonatal Resuscitation (Aziz et al, Pediatrics 2021;147 Suppl 1:e2020038505E)

nrp_epinephrine_endotracheal.doc: Part 5: Neonatal Resuscitation, 2025 AHA/AAP Guidelines (Lee et al, Circulation 2025;152(suppl 2):S385-S423, doi:10.1161/CIR.0000000000001367)
nrp_epinephrine_endotracheal.says: Endotracheal epinephrine at a larger dose is reasonable while access is obtained (2a, C-LD); if the response is inadequate give an intravascular dose as soon as access is in, regardless of the interval (2a, B-NR). 0.01-0.03 mg/kg is an inadequate endotracheal dose; once the UVC is in, use it. |  | 0.05-0.1 mg/kg down the tube.
nrp_epinephrine_endotracheal.changedIn2025: Both upgraded from 2b C-LD (2020) to 2a. 2020 AHA/AAP Part 5 Neonatal Resuscitation (Aziz et al, Pediatrics 2021;147 Suppl 1:e2020038505E)

epinephrine_shockable_timing.doc: Part 9: Adult Advanced Life Support, 2025 AHA Guidelines for CPR and ECC (Wigginton et al, Circulation 2025;152(suppl 2):S538-S577, doi:10.1161/CIR.0000000000001376)
epinephrine_shockable_timing.section: 10 Vasopressor Medications, rec 4 and supportive text; Figure 2
epinephrine_shockable_timing.says: In VF/pVT, defibrillate first; give epinephrine only after the initial shocks have failed (algorithm: after the 2nd shock). One in-hospital study found lower survival where epinephrine often came before the first shock. | After initial defibrillation attempts fail (after the 2nd shock in the algorithm)
epinephrine_shockable_timing.changedIn2025: Upgraded from 2b C-LD (2020) to 2a B-NR. 2020 AHA Part 3 Adult BLS/ALS (Panchal et al, Circulation 2020;142:S366-S468, doi:10.1161/CIR.0000000000000916)

pals_epinephrine_shockable_timing.doc: Part 8: Pediatric Advanced Life Support, 2025 AHA/AAP Guidelines (Lasa et al, Circulation 2025;152(suppl 2):S479-S537, doi:10.1161/CIR.0000000000001368)
pals_epinephrine_shockable_timing.section: 7.2 Drug Administration During Cardiac Arrest, rec 2
pals_epinephrine_shockable_timing.says: In a shockable arrest give epinephrine after 2 defibrillation attempts, or sooner only if rapid defibrillation is not possible. |
pals_epinephrine_shockable_timing.changedIn2025: New in 2025 (2020 had one timing recommendation for all rhythms). 2020 AHA Part 4 Pediatric BLS/ALS (Topjian et al, Circulation 2020;142:S469-S523, doi:10.1161/CIR.0000000000000901)

polymorphic_vt_normal_qt.doc: Part 9: Adult Advanced Life Support, 2025 AHA Guidelines for CPR and ECC (Wigginton et al, Circulation 2025;152(suppl 2):S538-S577, doi:10.1161/CIR.0000000000001376)
polymorphic_vt_normal_qt.says: IV lidocaine, amiodarone and treatment of myocardial ischaemia may be considered (2b, C-LD). Routine magnesium is not recommended when the QT is normal (3: No Benefit, C-LD). | Magnesium only if the QT is long

verapamil_diltiazem_wct.doc: Part 9: Adult Advanced Life Support, 2025 AHA Guidelines for CPR and ECC (Wigginton et al, Circulation 2025;152(suppl 2):S538-S577, doi:10.1161/CIR.0000000000001376)
verapamil_diltiazem_wct.section: 15 Wide-Complex Tachycardia, rec 5 and supportive text
verapamil_diltiazem_wct.says: Verapamil and diltiazem should not be given for wide-complex tachycardia: they will not stop VT and can cause profound hypotension, shock and arrest. |
verapamil_diltiazem_wct.changedIn2025: 2020 named verapamil only, with an exception for known SVT without an accessory pathway; 2025 adds diltiazem and drops the exception. 2020 AHA Part 3 Adult BLS/ALS (Panchal et al, Circulation 2020;142:S366-S468, doi:10.1161/CIR.0000000000000916)

nrp_volume.doc: Part 5: Neonatal Resuscitation, 2025 AHA/AAP Guidelines (Lee et al, Circulation 2025;152(suppl 2):S385-S423, doi:10.1161/CIR.0000000000001367)
nrp_volume.section: 16 Volume Expansion, recs 1-2 and supportive text; Figure 2
nrp_volume.says: A volume expander may be reasonable when history/exam suggest hypovolaemia (pallor, weak pulses, persistent HR <60). If HR stays <60 after epinephrine, the algorithm says consider hypovolaemia and pneumothorax. |  | Normal saline or blood 10-20 mL/kg, over 5-10 min; repeat if inadequate response.

pals_svt_antiarrhythmics.doc: Part 8: Pediatric Advanced Life Support, 2025 AHA/AAP Guidelines (Lasa et al, Circulation 2025;152(suppl 2):S479-S537, doi:10.1161/CIR.0000000000001368)
pals_svt_antiarrhythmics.section: 19.1 Treatment of SVT With a Pulse, recs 3 and 5
pals_svt_antiarrhythmics.says: Only if SVT with compromise has failed vagal manoeuvres, adenosine and cardioversion AND no expert is available may IV procainamide, amiodarone or sotalol be considered. Stable SVT unresponsive to vagal/adenosine: expert consultation (1, C-EO). |
pals_svt_antiarrhythmics.changedIn2025: Sotalol added in 2025 (2020 named procainamide or amiodarone). 2020 AHA Part 4 Pediatric BLS/ALS (Topjian et al, Circulation 2020;142:S469-S523, doi:10.1161/CIR.0000000000000901)

calcium_betablocker_poisoning.doc: Part 10: Adult and Pediatric Special Circumstances of Resuscitation, 2025 AHA Guidelines (Cao et al, Circulation 2025;152(suppl 2):S578-S672, doi:10.1161/CIR.0000000000001380)
calcium_betablocker_poisoning.says: Calcium may be reasonable (2b, C-EO). Stronger: vasopressors (1, C-EO), high-dose insulin for refractory hypotension (1, C-LD), glucagon bolus plus infusion (2a, C-LD). |  | Glucagon 2-10 mg (child 0.05-0.15 mg/kg), infusion 1-15 mg/h (Table 4).

calcium_hypermagnesemia.doc: Part 10: Adult and Pediatric Special Circumstances of Resuscitation, 2025 AHA Guidelines (Cao et al, Circulation 2025;152(suppl 2):S578-S672, doi:10.1161/CIR.0000000000001380)
calcium_hypermagnesemia.section: 19.3 Pregnant Patients in Cardiac Arrest, rec 8
calcium_hypermagnesemia.says: Giving calcium to a pregnant patient who arrests while receiving IV magnesium sulfate is reasonable. |
calcium_hypermagnesemia.changedIn2025: 2020 had a general hypermagnesemia rec (empirical IV calcium, 2b C-EO); 2025 keeps only the pregnancy/magnesium-infusion version at 2a. 2020 AHA Part 3 Adult BLS/ALS (Panchal et al, Circulation 2020;142:S366-S468, doi:10.1161/CIR.0000000000000916)

magnesium_hypomagnesemia.doc: 2020 AHA Part 3 Adult BLS/ALS (Panchal et al, Circulation 2020;142:S366-S468, doi:10.1161/CIR.0000000000000916)
magnesium_hypomagnesemia.section: Electrolyte Abnormalities in Cardiac Arrest, rec 2
magnesium_hypomagnesemia.says: 2020: IV magnesium is recommended in addition to standard ACLS for arrest from severe hypomagnesemia. The 2025 Parts 9-10 contain no hypomagnesemia recommendation (searched), so the 2020 statement has not been restated. |
magnesium_hypomagnesemia.changedIn2025: Not restated in the 2025 guidelines (absent from Parts 9 and 10).
